investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption was also unavailable (No preemption victims found). Because no pod reached a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and the probe returned no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes; if those nodes are at capacity there is no fallback, and the four remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.

Tertiary — a recent scale-down or node failure may have reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool from a larger count to exactly two nodes, shrinking total VM slot capacity below the demand level required for concurrent eval probes.

Lower confidence — a misconfigured resource request quantity in the pod spec (requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than available per node) could cause premature exhaustion even with low concurrent usage; this cannot be confirmed without the pod spec.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). Preemption was also unavailable (No preemption victims found). Because no pod reached a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, and the probe returned no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available on any node. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both report Insufficient capacity; the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent with type "remote") from ever provisioning an agent, so no runtime response is produced and all required evidence is absent. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, which may indicate a node label was removed, a taint was added, or the pod spec's affinity rules were tightened. This would reduce the eligible node pool from 6 to 2, amplifying any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — a resource leak or stuck pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously scheduled remote-agent pods (e.g., from prior eval runs or user sessions) may not have been cleaned up, exhausting the finite VM resource pool. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), but cleanup may have failed in earlier runs.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote-agent pods than is currently demanded, and no autoscaling or node-pool expansion is available for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type.
